problem_motivation.content: Predicting stress/strain fields is needed because repeated FEM simulations over large composite design spaces are prohibitively expensive.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: The prediction of stress and strain fields in composite materials from microstructural geometry has emerged as a key research direction in data-driven mechanics, driven by the prohibitive computational cost of repeated finite element method (FEM) simulations [7] across large composite design spaces.

prior_approach.content: Yang et al. used a conditional GAN to predict stress and strain fields for two-phase composite geometries.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The dataset has been obtained from Yang et al.[1] where a conditional GAN model was trained for predicting stress and strain fields across a range of two-phase composite geometries.

prior_approach.content: Earlier work used CNNs as FEM surrogates with high accuracy.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Early work demonstrated that convolutional neural networks could serve as efficient surrogates for FEM at high accuracy.

prior_approach.content: SCSNet and StressNet were proposed as CNN architectures for predicting von Mises stress fields from geometry, loading, and boundary conditions.
prior_approach.evidence_span: A foundational benchmark was established in [6], proposing SCSNet and StressNet two CNN architectures for predicting von Mises stress fields in 2D linear elastic cantilevered structures from geometry, loading, and boundary condition inputs

prior_approach.content: A U-Net encoder-decoder was proposed for predicting von Mises stress fields in fiber-reinforced composites.
prior_approach.evidence_span: A U-Net encoder-decoder architecture was pro- posed in [5, 15] for von Mises stress field prediction in fiber- reinforced composites

prior_approach.content: A conditional GAN with a U-Net generator and PatchGAN discriminator was trained on FEM data to predict stress and plastic strain fields from geometry images.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The image-to-image translation paradigm for composite field prediction was advanced in [1], where a conditional GAN comprising a U-Net generator and PatchGAN discriminator was trained to predict von Mises stress and plastic strain fields in two-phase hierarchical composites directly from 2D geometry images, using FEM simulations in Abaqus as ground truth across 2,000 randomly generated composite geometries.

prior_approach.content: A follow-up study extended the model to predict full stress and strain tensor components and tuned data statistics for better generalization.
prior_approach.evidence_span: A follow-up study [2] extended this to predict complete stress and strain tensor components across all field directions, incorporating data statistics tuning to improve generalization across varying constituent ratios under limited training data.

prior_approach.content: A Fourier Neural Operator was proposed for geometry-to-field mapping in the frequency domain.
prior_approach.evidence_span: A Fourier Neural Operator framework was proposed in [3] that oper- ates in the frequency domain rather than the pixel domain

prior_approach.content: A graph neural network framework used FEM-mesh-to-graph correspondence to predict deformation, stress, and strain fields.
prior_approach.evidence_span: A graph neural network framework was proposed in [4] that exploits the natural correspondence between FEM meshes and graphs, predicting deformation, stress and strain fields across fiber composites, stratified composites and lattice metamaterials

prior_approach.content: A hybrid CNN-Transformer for small-data settings was proposed using progressive tokenization, feature supplementation, and a convolutional shortcut.
prior_approach.evidence_span: A hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture for small data paradigms was proposed in [10], incorporating progres- sive tokenization with feature supplementation and a convolu- tional prediction module shortcut, enabling effective training without large-scale pre-training.

prior_approach.content: The dataset was generated by Yang et al. using FEM simulations in Abaqus.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The dataset used in this work is sourced from Yang et al. [1], where it was generated through finite element method (FEM) simulations using the commercial Abaqus software.

prior_approach.content: The dataset was taken from Yang et al. and generated using FEM simulations in Abaqus.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The dataset used in this work is sourced from Yang et al. [1], where it was generated through finite element method (FEM) simulations using the commercial Abaqus software.

prior_limitation.content: Existing architectures rely on convolutional inductive biases that limit their ability to model long-range spatial dependencies, especially for non-local load transfer paths.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Despite this progression, a common limitation across the above architectures is their reliance on convolutional inductive biases local receptive fields and translational equivariance which constrain the model’s capacity to capture long-range spatial dependencies in stress and strain fields, particularly for geometries with non-local load transfer paths.

prior_limitation.content: Standard Vision Transformers need large training datasets, which does not fit the small FEM-generated datasets used in computational mechanics.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, standard Vision Transformers require large training datasets to converge effectively, which is incompatible with the small FEM-generated datasets typical of computational mechanics.
